findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "business" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contract-terminator, accessibility-patcher, open-badges-verifier, redact-text, property-violations-history, locale-number, id-kind, date-claim-check, gtin-hierarchy, platform-text-fit, font-face-css · Private data: audit-public-record, open-badges-verifier, property-violations-history, locale-number, date-claim-check, credential-coverage, checksum, tax-id-format, subtitle-lint, font-face-css, metar-parse, manual-applicability, document-supersession, transcribe-url, vendor-verification · Public sink: lead-enrichment, medical-bill-auditor, contract-terminator, filing-integrity-check, redact-text, minor-units, allocate, id-kind, business-deadline, dst-check, date-claim-check, time-bucket-check, gtin-hierarchy, platform-text-fit, site-access-check · Destructive: reconcile-ledger, id-kind, checksum, tax-id-format, timecode-convert, font-convert, electrical-calc, company-filing-monitor.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
